text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Thursday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Prime Minister Andris Shkele has not said he his ready to form a new government he told journalists after a regular meeting with President Guntis Ulmanis.
- Newly-appointed Finance Minister Vassily Melnik tendered his resignation to Shkele, who accepted it.
- The Democratic Party Saimnieks, the Farmer's Union, the Christian Democrats Union, LNNK and the movement For People and Justice will call on Ulmanis to recall Shkele to form a new government.

- Latvia's Way decided not to nominate its own candidate and start consultations with Saimnieks, who backed Shkele and Fatherland & Freedom, who earlier proposed Economy Minister Gundar Krasts as new PM. But Fatherland and Freedom said it would not insist on its candidate unless supported by at least one of the major parties.

- President Ulmanis sent a letter to the parliament speaker asking for a revision of recent amendments to the law on harbours, requiring specialised maritime education from candidates to the post of port chief manager.
- The economic crimes police neither confirms nor denies any connection between Vassily Melnik, controversial new finance minister, and the smuggled alcohol, arrested last December.
- Liepaja became the first city in the Baltics to open a business promotion centre. It was assisted by the Latvian Development agency, the U.S. Peace Corps and the U.S. embassy.

- President of the Latvian Shipping Company, Peteris Avotinsh, is likely to be considered for dismissal at a board meeting on Friday, board chairman Druvis Skulte said. A new finance director is expected to start working for the company on February 1. Norwegian Sten Forland will have the status of vice-president of the company.
- Some six percent of state-owned flats were privatised in 1996, the Commission for Appartment Privatisation says. Another 25 percent are expected to be sold in 1997.
